static_traits.name: Liu Haili
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no psychotherapy received in the past; has not yet reported similar problems before.
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and experiences concretely; skeptical attitude toward change, average cooperativeness; clear logic; speech rate not mentioned; feeling shame and discomfort when intimate topics arise, tending to avoid.

basic_info.main_problem: I believe that because I am taller than all the boys in my class, I can never date, which makes me feel lonely and socially isolated.
basic_info.core_demands: I recently realized my avoidance of social interactions and dating opportunities is negatively affecting my mental health and quality of life.
growth_experiences: Starting in early adolescence being teased by classmates about height, gradually forming strong unease and inferiority. In social situations (such as when classmates gather or talk about relationships) more easily triggered discomfort and withdrawal; over time, increasing social avoidance and avoidance of dating opportunities out of fear of rejection and ridicule, leading to loneliness and reduced daily interaction.

core_beliefs: I do not fit in / am not accepted by others (because of height)

special_situations.event: In school social settings, when classmates talk about dating or pair up
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am taller than boys, boys will not like me; not being liked means I can never date
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding social situations and dating opportunities, telling myself 'I'm better off alone' to reduce disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I can never get a date anyway, going will only lead to being rejected.

special_situations.event: Observing boys in class interacting more with shorter girls
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If boys interact more with shorter girls, it means all boys only like short girls
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reducing contact with boys, shrinking the social circle to avoid being compared or negated again
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: All boys like shorter girls, I have no chance.

special_situations.event: Recalls past experiences of being laughed at by classmates for height
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Being teased proves I am flawed; if I approach others again, I will be humiliated and rejected again
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying not to participate in dating topics, lowering self-exposure to avoid shame
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will be teased/rejected again, better not to try.

special_situations.event: Occasionally a boy takes the initiative to talk to me
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Even if the other person speaks, it is only out of politeness, and in the end they will still reject me
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignoring or downplaying these positive cues, not engaging deeply to protect myself from being hurt
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This does not count, they are not really interested in me.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be liked, accepted, and to build intimate relationships
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being rejected, ridiculed, and humiliated again
defense_goal: Reducing the risk of being rejected by avoiding socializing and lowering expectations
Uses the rationale 'I am better off alone' to maintain a sense of psychological safety

object_relations.self_representation: Out of place, a 'tall girl' easily rejected
object_relations.object_representation: Mockers/rejecters who are picky and prefer 'short ones'

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes testing hypotheses or exploring more balanced possibilities (e.g.: inviting imagining different outcomes)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: If holding hope will lead to greater disappointment, the counselor's encouragement equals forcing me to face failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Tone gentle but reserved, emphasizes 'worrying about being disappointed', uses conditional sentences and vague expressions (such as 'maybe' and 'perhaps'), avoids clear commitments.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When asked whether willing to try social small goals or behavioral experiments
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Rather than trying and being rejected, telling myself 'I'm better off alone'
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using a self-comforting and justifying tone (such as 'this is better/easier for me'), downplaying risks, avoiding detailed commitments.

manifestations: Feeling out of place and isolated in social situations
Avoids dating and social interaction, believes 'I am better off alone'
Unwilling to discuss troubles with family or friends, feeling embarrassed and ashamed
outcomes: Persistent sense of loneliness and social isolation
Decreased sense of self-worth and negative anticipation

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Treating 'all boys like shorter girls' as a self-evident rule
Inferring from this that one 'can never date', rejecting counterexamples

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Has the impulse to reach out to others but tells oneself 'forget it, I am better off alone'
When someone initiates a conversation, minimizes responses and avoids going deeper, so as not to bear possible rejection

exception_events.target_problem: In social situations at school, Hai Li usually avoids interacting with boys out of worry about being rejected because of height, then feels even lonelier.
exception_events.unique_outcome: A few times in campus interactions, boys took the initiative to talk to Hai Li; although at the time she did not pay much attention due to worry about being rejected, positive signs inconsistent with her prediction that 'no one will pay attention to me' did appear.
exception_events.reason: Clues: the other party initiated, the setting was more casual, the interaction atmosphere was safer, providing real feedback contradicting the existing belief.

positive_force: Can notice and name one's negative thinking and avoidance patterns
Willing to try small, controllable goals (such as one brief exchange with a new classmate)
In reality there are clues of others proactively approaching, which can serve as counterevidence and resources
negative_force: Catastrophizing, overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, and predicting the future show marked cognitive biases
The core belief 'I cannot be loved/accepted' reinforcing self-denial
Social and dating avoidance maintaining the vicious cycle of anxiety and loneliness
Shame and discomfort about disclosing to and seeking help from family and friends, insufficient use of social support

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding social interaction and dating-related situations with classmates (especially boys)
antecedent: At school social occasions or when discussing romantic topics
When seeing boys interact with shorter girls
When recalling being mocked for my height in the past
target_behavior.core_reason: Strong fear of being rejected and shame, accompanied by catastrophizing, overgeneralization, and black-and-white thinking, plus the deep belief 'I cannot be loved/accepted'.
target_behavior.function: Avoiding potential rejection and shame, reducing anxiety and discomfort in the short term
target_behavior.consequence: Fewer social opportunities, increased sense of loneliness, negative beliefs further reinforced, daily interaction and quality of life impaired

target_behavior.behavior: Repeated negative automatic thoughts (such as 'I can never date')
antecedent: Thinking about relationship issues when Being alone
When peers pair up or talk about dating
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases such as predicting the future, mind-reading inferences, and mental filtering maintaining a negative interpretation framework, stemming from emotional reasoning about being teased.
target_behavior.function: Self-protection by lowering expectations, avoiding the pain of dashed hopes
target_behavior.consequence: Low mood and decreased drive, further intensifying avoidance and social withdrawal
